name: Pale Ossuary
specific_features: Derelict space station in orbit, hull breached in a perfect spiral
description: Pale Ossuary is a moon-sized shard of chalk-white rock hanging in the outer dark, its surface so densely cratered that no original terrain survives. The lack of atmosphere means every impact of the last four billion years is preserved in perfect detail—a fossil record written in stone and shadow. Platinum-bearing ejecta gives its brightest craters a faint metallic glitter under the distant sun.

Nothing moves here, ever. The vacuum carries neither sound nor scent, and footprints pressed into the powdery regolith will outlast the civilization that made them. The sun itself is just the brightest star in a black sky, casting knife-edged shadows that swing across the wastes in slow, silent procession.

The derelict station in low orbit predates every charted power in the sector. Its hull is opened by a single spiral wound, as if some vast tool bored into it and withdrew, yet its interior compartments remain pressurized behind sealed bulkheads. Salvage crews who boarded it describe corridors lined with rows of empty stasis pods, each labeled in an unknown script with what translators suspect are names.

Rumors persist that one pod at the station's core is not empty. Independent miners now avoid Pale Ossuary's orbit entirely, claiming the station's running lights cycle on for six seconds each time its shadow crosses the terminator below. Whoever those pods were built to hold, something may still be waiting for them to open—and the platinum rush is bringing more ships every month.
